summary: Configured node1 to require new user passwords be at least 12 characters with at least 3 character classes, verified enforcement (rejects short/low-diversity passwords, accepts compliant ones) both before and after a full node restart, then cleaned up test users.
actions_performed: Inspected /etc/security/pwquality.conf and PAM system-auth/password-auth wiring on node1 (RHEL 7.9, pam_pwquality already active via requisite)

Created test user pwtestuser and verified via real PAM password-change flow (su + passwd) that: <11-char password rejected, 12+ char password with only 2 classes rejected, 12+ char password with 3 classes accepted
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, uptime -s, pwquality.conf content, PAM config
Issued backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' on node1 so the ack returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again; confirmed new boot_id and fresh uptime -s, proving an actual restart occurred
Re-verified pwquality.conf and PAM config persisted post-restart
Re-ran full live enforcement test post-restart with a second test user (pwtestuser2): weak/2-class password rejected, compliant 3-class 13-char password accepted
Deleted pwtestuser2 and confirmed both test users no longer exist

evidence.requirement: minlen=12 and minclass=3 configured on node1
evidence.summary: pwquality.conf shows minlen=12 and minclass=3 both immediately after edit and again after the node restart, proving the setting is in place and persistent.

evidence.requirement: Policy actually enforced for new user passwords (length + character classes)
evidence.summary: Live passwd attempts via PAM as a non-root user show short passwords and passwords with fewer than 3 character classes are rejected with pwquality errors, while a 12+ character password with 3 classes is accepted (exit 0).
Captured pre-restart boot_id (d7a80301-...), uptime -s, and confirmed pwquality.conf/PAM config were correctly in place before disrupting the node.
Backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' returned REBOOT_ACK immediately, before the node went unreachable.

First poll after reboot command failed with connection timeout (node down); subsequent poll succeeded with a new boot_id (6930b99c-...) and fresh uptime -s (2026-09-04 23:34:32), differing from the pre-restart boot_id, proving a real restart.

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required config and live enforcement
evidence.summary: After restart, pwquality.conf and PAM wiring were intact, and a fresh live PAM password-change test again rejected a non-compliant password and accepted a compliant one; test users were then removed, confirmed via failed 'id' lookups.
